claims.statement: EU guidance permits food no longer marketable for human consumption, including unsold bread and broken biscuits, to enter animal feed where it is safe and all feed rules are met.
Feed-chain operators face registration or approval, hygiene, HACCP, traceability, safety and labelling duties; a digital exchange does not remove those duties.

Packaging contamination prevents direct feed use, and streams containing animal-origin material enter additional animal-by-product rules; eligibility therefore cannot be granted generically to a bakery, brewery or factory.

Poland publishes a register of establishments approved or registered under feed-hygiene rules, making recipient-status checks technically possible but not guaranteeing that a listed operator will accept a particular stream.
Poland already has IUNGO sourcing food-sector products and selling specified feed materials, while Trotec is building a former-food processing factory in Przasnysz.
Direct incumbents bundle containers, weighing, registration, processing, technical integration, compliance advice and logistics, so a thin matching layer has no evidenced advantage by itself.
No reviewed direct incumbent page publishes a comparable generator subscription or transaction take rate; willingness to pay 500-1500 PLN per stream monthly remains unknown.

contrary_evidence: IUNGO has operated in Poland since 2004 and already sources food-sector products, processes them and sells specified feed materials.
Trotec is constructing a Polish factory and offers an integrated processing, logistics, sensor, data and compliance service rather than a software-only exchange.
FeedValid similarly supplies containers, transport, weighing and registration, indicating that operational execution is part of the incumbent value proposition.
EU food-use hierarchy prioritises prevention and human redistribution before feed where food remains suitable for people.
A successful introduction can be disintermediated when generator and processor contract directly.

economics.acquisition_route: Approach one independent registered processor from the public Polish register as the anchor customer, qualify only streams it conditionally pre-accepts, and have that processor invite three to five generators under recurring offtake contracts. This replaces simultaneous two-sided prospecting with one enterprise sale and supplier enablement, but processor commitment and generator adoption remain unproven.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast: 300 active contracted streams at 1000 PLN monthly would produce 3.6 million PLN annual software revenue without a transaction take rate. At 25% EBITDA and a 6x multiple, that is 5.4 million PLN enterprise value; with 100% founder ownership and no debt it would approximate 5.4 million PLN founder equity before tax and illiquidity, without double-counting distributions. Reaching that scale over 5-7 years would require multiple renewing processors, continuing record rights and contribution margins that are all unvalidated.
economics.founder_time: Initially 15-25 hours weekly for product work, one anchor-processor sale and bounded supplier onboarding. Classification, HACCP, sampling, transport, acceptance, recall and emergency decisions must remain with the licensed processor or other qualified operators; assuming those duties would exceed the founder's limit.
economics.gross_margin_basis: A processor-paid software licence could retain the unvalidated 65-80% contribution-margin target only if laboratories, transport, storage, processing, product liability and routine supplier support remain contractually with the processor and generators. Configuration and onboarding effort must be measured because it may make the offer service-heavy.
economics.payback: Not established. As a mechanical sensitivity, 20 processor-contracted active streams at 1000 PLN monthly and 65% contribution would yield 13000 PLN monthly before fixed costs and founder labour, nominally covering 60000 PLN in about five months after that scale is reached. This excludes enterprise sales time, onboarding cost, churn and any unpaid pilot period, and neither price nor adoption is validated.
economics.pricing: Test a processor-paid monthly licence of 500-1500 PLN per active recurring stream after a no-fee pilot, with no transaction take rate. This reassigns the original unvalidated fee range to the processor; no reviewed source establishes that a processor will pay it.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Renewal would depend on the processor requiring the shared intake record throughout each active recurring offtake contract and continuing to use its qualification, forecast, exception and recall history. That design reduces match-and-bypass exposure but concentrates churn risk in the anchor processor and remains unvalidated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A contract-permissioned longitudinal history of stream specifications, tests, acceptances, volumes and rejection reasons accumulated as each processor onboards contracted generators, but only if the processor grants lawful continuing record rights and keeps the software in the recurring workflow.
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish registered feed processors that want to standardize intake of recurring, separately stored plant-only former-food streams; their contracted food-manufacturer suppliers use the processor-mandated workflow rather than forming a second customer side.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell to one registered processor from the finite public register, then let that processor distribute the workflow by inviting generators covered by its conditional recurring offtake contracts; laboratories and associations remain referral channels rather than a second marketplace side.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A processor-branded intake and compliance operating system for generator onboarding, stream qualification records, batch and lab evidence, forecast volumes, acceptance and exception logs, and recall-ready exports, sold as recurring software per active contracted stream; no matching marketplace or transaction take rate, and physical handling remains with licensed operators.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The registered processor is the hypothesized payer, owing a recurring software licence after it activates a conditionally accepted stream under an offtake contract; willingness to pay and the proposed per-stream price remain unvalidated.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A registered processor wants recurring former-food input but must qualify each generator stream, bind eligibility and evidence to an offtake relationship, and maintain traceable acceptance, forecast, exception and recall records before and throughout repeated intake.

founder_fit: The data, workflow, traceability and exception-analysis product fits the founder's quantitative and AI skills.
One anchor processor and three to five invited generators create a bounded pilot compatible with the founder's 5-hour daily limit if counterparties retain physical and safety duties.
A processor-led enterprise sale avoids public-facing consumer marketing, but still requires a concentrated trust-building relationship and qualified feed-law and veterinary support.
FMCG adjacency is useful only through public knowledge and newly obtained customer data; employer information must not be used.

redesign.economic_effect: Replacing the two-sided exchange and transaction take rate with a processor-paid recurring software licence changes the intended acquisition path to one anchor processor plus its invited generators, could reduce post-match bypass exposure, and keeps the platform asset-light. It also concentrates revenue and renewal risk in each processor, leaves willingness to pay and adoption unvalidated, and does not improve transport, processing or stream-level economics.

risks: Feed contamination, packaging residue or misclassification could harm animals or trigger a recall.
Animal-origin ingredients can move a stream into stricter animal-by-product controls.
Transport and drying economics can overwhelm the value of low-price feed materials.
Strong processors can bundle the record-keeping feature or bypass the exchange.
Assuming title, custody or product responsibility would increase regulatory, insurance and capital exposure.
Part-time operation is incompatible with emergency logistics or safety decisions unless those duties remain with qualified partners.
A processor can bundle or replicate the redesigned record-keeping product, and dependence on one anchor creates customer-concentration risk.
A processor may refuse to mandate an independent workflow or grant continuing rights to its stream history, preventing the proposed retention and data advantage.
Generators may not maintain the record consistently even when invited by a processor, increasing onboarding and support effort.

structure.commercial_archetype: Processor-anchored B2B intake and compliance operating system
structure.control_point: The processor-mandated recurring intake record embedded in generator offtake contracts, together with contractually permitted continuity of the longitudinal stream history
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed processor willing to pay, require the workflow in supplier relationships and grant lawful continuing record rights while retaining operational and safety responsibility

thesis: A processor-anchored intake and compliance operating system can let one registered feed processor conditionally onboard recurring, plant-only former-food streams and require generators to maintain stream-specific classification, test and traceability records through recurring offtake contracts. The processor, rather than the generator or a transaction, is the hypothesized payer and onboarding channel, while physical handling and safety decisions remain with qualified operators. Existing incumbents already integrate these functions, and no evidence yet shows that a processor will pay for, mandate or grant durable record rights to an independent software layer.
title: Processor-Anchored Former-Food Intake OS
uncertainties: How many Polish generators have recurring eligible volumes not already contracted to processors or waste operators.
Which exact plant-only stream classes processors will pre-accept and at what minimum volume, radius and specification.
Whether a generator or processor will pay a recurring software fee after the first match.
Actual laboratory frequency, rejection rate, transport cost, feed-equivalent price and spoilage window by stream.
Whether the platform itself would be treated as a feed business operator or broker under the intended contractual flow.
Whether insurers and counterparties will accept the proposed allocation of contamination, recall and mislabelling liability.
Whether a registered processor will pay the redesigned recurring software fee, require generators to use the workflow and renew after the pilot.
Whether a processor will grant lawful continuing rights to retain and use the stream history if the commercial relationship ends.
Paid-pilot conversion, enterprise sales cycle, supplier onboarding effort, churn and contribution margin.
